title: China Just Wrote 18 Tasks for AI and Jobs - What It Means for Your Career
content:
China just told its whole government how to protect jobs from AI. And there is a career lesson in it for all of us.
On October twenty third, China's State Council released new guidelines on adapting to AI.
They set out EIGHTEEN TASKS in six areas.
The goal is to use AI to create jobs, while reducing the jobs it replaces.
One detail stood out to me.
For AI projects that could cause major job disruption in some sectors, the guidelines call for an EMPLOYMENT RISK ASSESSMENT during the project review.
They also encourage companies to tell affected workers early and help them move into new roles.
Now the career part.
The guidelines call for faster creation of new occupations, and they name roles like AI TRAINERS, AI engineering technicians and digital managers.
An earlier government article says China added seventy two new occupations over the past five years, including AI TRAINERS.
Why should you care if you do not live in China?
Because when a government writes job titles into policy, those skills stop being a trend. They become a category employers hire for.
So here is how to use this.
Step one. Pick one AI-adjacent role, like AI trainer, AI operations, or AI solutions engineer.
Step two. Learn the core skill behind it: writing clear instructions, checking AI output, and connecting AI to real business data.
Step three. Build one small project you can show, like a document question-answering tool for a real use case.
Say you work in HR. You build a simple assistant that answers policy questions from your company handbook, and you test its answers every week.
Now you are not just in HR. You are the person who runs AI for HR.
Here's my take. AI will not hand out new jobs. It will hand them to the people who PREPARED EARLY.
Follow for your daily AI update.
